items.title: `reactive::zip_some`, `ui::when_all_some` and `SignalCell<(A, B)>::unzip`: wait for several `Flow<Option<..>>` at once, so a view handles the negative states in ONE place and its body reads plain values
items.body:
Generic over `Option` by the owner's ruling (not over `TransientState`): a `TransientState` flow reaches it through `.ready()`, a mirror through `.latest()`, a plain `Option` flow as it is.

1. `reactive::zip_some((a, b, ..))`: takes a tuple of `Flow<Option<T>>`, answers `Flow<Option<(A, B, ..)>>` - `Some` only when every part is. VALUE level: stateless, no owner, composes with `.derive`/`.effect`/`.distinct`. It is `combine` + `Option::zip` written once, on `combine`'s per-arity mechanism.

2. `ui::when_all_some((a, b, ..), |(a, b, ..)| ..)` on BOTH ui twins (`std_twin_parity`): `when_some(zip_some(sources), ..)` plus the split - the body takes ONE parameter, a tuple of `SignalCell`s (`(SignalCell<A>, SignalCell<B>)`), destructured at the call site. The cells are created under the body's owner when everything turns `Some`, updated IN PLACE while it stays `Some` (the body is not rebuilt on a payload change, as `when_some`), and released when any part goes `None`. One parameter per element is B521, later.

3. `SignalCell<(A, B)>::unzip(): (SignalCell<A>, SignalCell<B>)` (arity as `combine`) for the non-view case; needs an owner context, like `.cell()`.

NOT built, by ruling: a `zip` answering `Flow<Option<(Flow<A>, Flow<B>)>>` - a pipe cannot travel through a flow, so the parts would have to be cells, and a free-standing lazy stage has no owner for them (each consumer would mint its own set).

Dependent parts need nothing new: `let author = message.and_then(|m| m.author.user()); when_all_some((message, author), ..)`.

Acceptance: kolt's message row written with it (a patch for the owner); pins for in-place update, release on `None`, and the server twin's single render; docs in the std reactive and ui pages.

items.title: a body closure with ONE PARAMETER PER TUPLE ELEMENT for tuple-taking combinators (`when_all_some((a, b), \|a, b\| ..)` instead of `\|(a, b)\| ..`)
items.body: A152 ships `when_all_some` with a single tuple parameter, destructured at the call site. This item is the spread form: either per-arity overloads whose closure takes N parameters, or a general rule that a closure of N parameters is accepted where a closure of one N-tuple is expected. Decide which (the general rule also touches `combine(..).derive(\|(a, b)\| ..)`), and whether the two-character saving is worth a solver rule at all - measure against A152's call sites in kolt first.
